title: Banks vs Fintech for International Payments in India: Which Is Better?
summary: Banks vs fintech: Which is better for receiving international payments in India? Compare transaction fees, exchange rates, settlement time and services.
body_markdown:
## How Do Fintech Platforms Handle International Payments?


A fintech payment platform is a technology-led company that is built to move money across borders. It does not offer the full range of a bank, such as loans or branches. Instead, you sign up online, get your account details and manage your payments from one dashboard or app.


Infinity is also a fintech payment platform. It is AD-1 certified and RBI-regulated, and it is built for Indian freelancers, exporters and startup founders who receive international payments.


Here is how it usually works. You sign up and complete KYC. The platform gives you account details in currencies such as USD, GBP or EUR. You share these details with your client. Your client sends money to those details, and the platform credits you after conversion, with the documents ready.


Because the platform is built for this one job, the experience is designed around clarity. You can see the fees upfront and track the payment.


*Read more:*[Infinity vs ICICI Bank: Which Is Better for International Payments?](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/infinity-vs-icici-bank-international-payments-exporters)


### 1.What are the strengths of fintech platforms?


-


**Transparent pricing:** The fee is clear before you receive the payment.


-


**Faster settlement:** Money often reaches you in a day, not several days.


-


**Digital onboarding:** Signing up and verification happen online.


-


**Tracking and notifications:** You can see the status of your payment.


-


**Automatic documents:** The platform generates the paperwork for you.


### 2.What are the limitations of fintech platforms?


It is fair to look at both sides. A fintech platform is not a full bank, so you will still need an Indian bank account to receive rupees. Features, limits and pricing differ from one platform to another, so it is worth checking the details before you choose. And you should always confirm that the platform is authorised by the RBI. Look for AD-1 certification.

## Which Is Better for Freelancers, Exporters and Startup Founders?


For all three, a fintech platform is usually the better option for regular international payments, because you lose less money in fees and you get paid sooner. The right choice still depends on how you work.


### Which is better for freelancers?


Fintech platforms like Infinity are better for freelancers. You receive payments from clients in different countries, often in different currencies, and the amounts add up. Lower fees and faster settlement mean more money in your pocket and faster cash flow. A platform that gives you local bank details also makes it easy for your clients to pay you without confusion.


A bank can still work if you receive a payment only once or twice a year.


*Read more:*[Best International Payment Gateways for Indian Freelancers](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/international-payment-gateways-for-freelancers)


### Which is better for exporters?


Fintech platforms are better for exporters who receive payments regularly from overseas buyers. You deal with repeat transactions, so clear fees and quick settlement help you plan your cash flow. Automatic documents also save time, since you need proof of every inward payment for your records.


A bank may still be useful when you already have a trade finance or credit relationship with it and want to keep your payments in the same place.


*Read more:*[Best International Payment Gateway Providers for Exporters in India](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/international-payment-gateway-providers-for-exporters)


### Which is better for startup founders?


Fintech platforms are better for founders who receive money from international customers or clients. Founders move fast, and waiting several days for a payment affects everything from payroll to vendor bills. A platform that lets you hold a USD balance and convert whenever you choose also gives you control over when to convert.


*Read more:*[How to Receive International Payments in India as a Startup Founder](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/international-payments-india-startup-founders)


### When is a bank still the right choice?


A bank is the right choice when:


-


You receive international payments very rarely.


-


You want all your financial services in one place.


-


You already use your bank for trade finance, loans or credit, and prefer to keep things together.


-


You prefer in-person support at a branch.


Many people also use both. You can keep your regular bank account for everyday banking and use a fintech platform for international payments.

## FAQs


### Banks vs fintech for international payments in India: which is better?


For most freelancers, exporters and startup founders, fintech platforms are better. They usually charge lower and clearer fees, settle faster and generate documents automatically. Banks are a good fit for occasional transfers or when you want all your services in one place.


### Is fintech safe for receiving international payments in India?


Yes, when the platform is authorised. In India, platforms that handle cross-border payments need RBI authorisation. Infinity is AD-1 certified and RBI-regulated.


### Are fintech platforms regulated by RBI?


Yes, authorised fintech platforms that handle foreign exchange for cross-border payments are regulated by the RBI. You should check for AD-1 certification before you choose one.


### Do fintech platforms provide FIRA or FIRC?


Banks issue a FIRC on request. Fintech platforms usually issue a FIRA. Infinity auto-generates a FIRA for free with your payments.


### Why do banks charge more for international payments?


Banks often charge more because the payment passes through several steps, and each step can add a cost. These include the sender bank fee, intermediary bank charges, the inward remittance fee, the FX markup and GST. Together, they reduce the amount you finally receive.


### Can I use both a bank and a fintech platform?


Yes. You can keep your bank account for everyday banking and use a fintech platform like Infinity to receive international payments. You will still need your Indian bank account to receive rupees.


### How long does a bank take to receive an international payment?


A bank typically takes a few working days, often two to five, to credit an international payment. It can take longer if the payment passes through more intermediary banks or if extra details are needed. Infinity settles payments in 24 hours.
